title: SRFed: Mitigating Poisoning Attacks in Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning with Heterogeneous Data

C-a.quote: First, we design a decentralized efficient functional encryption (DEFE) scheme to support efficient model encryption and non-interactive decryption. DEFE also eliminates third-party reliance and defends against server-side inference attacks. Second, we develop a privacy-preserving defensive model aggregation mechanism based on DEFE. This mechanism filters poisonous models under Non-IID data by layer-wise projection and clusteringbased analysis.

THE ROW'S VALUE IS NOT ITS CODES -- IT FAILS THE PRIMARY THREE SEPARATE WAYS (C-a NO, C-b NO, C-d YES) -- IT IS THEOREM 6.2, WHICH IS AN EXTERNAL, INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED INSTANCE OF COMPOSITION INVARIANCE. The theorem proves that inserting an upstream transform (the DEFE noise perturbation) leaves the downstream detector's DECISIONS approximately unchanged, and the proof's stated conclusion is exactly that: the introduced perturbation does not affect model detection. That is the same object our Prop. prop:identification_full asks about, established by proof rather than by sweep. It sits beside Fed-DPRoC (which proves a GUARANTEE survives an upstream transform) and DDFed (which MEASURES a detector's effectiveness across upstream noise levels) as the third external treatment of the invariance question, and it is the closest of the three to what we formalize. A3 should cite all three together; this one is the analytic member of the trio. 

C-a = NO IS THE DECIDING CODE AND IT RESTS ON A GRANULARITY JUDGMENT THAT THE PRE-REGISTRATION NEVER OPERATIONALIZED. C-a asks for "two or more DISTINCT defense mechanisms"; "distinct" was frozen without a definition, and Amendment 3 governs PURPOSE, not granularity. Amendment 3 removes DEFE cleanly (its purpose is privacy), which leaves the layer-wise projection, the K-Means clustering, the cosine-similarity cluster ranking and the mean of the survivors. Counted finely that is four; counted as a defense mechanism it is ONE detector -- a single decision function computed in stages, emitting one 0/1 keep-mask. THE RULE I HAVE ACTUALLY BEEN APPLYING, STATED HERE BECAUSE THIS ROW FORCED IT, IS: a component is DISTINCT when it contributes an INDEPENDENT DISCRIMINATIVE SIGNAL OR AN INDEPENDENT DECISION about an update, and not when it is a stage in computing one signal. On that rule SRFed is one mechanism (projection is the feature, K-Means partitions it, the cosine ranking labels the partition, and there is exactly one verdict per client), whereas 2601.06466's auditing stack is three (a cluster-relative Mahalanobis score, a separate across-round trajectory score, and a three-way accept/down-weight/reject decision over three independently maintained thresholds).
